title: A Tuesday
subtitle: One ordinary day, from five in the morning to ten at night.
description: An A1 reading and listening text that brings together the people, times, rooms and food words from the other A1 readings in one ordinary day.
source: authored for this site; no source document
passage: I get up at five. I take a shower, I make coffee, and I leave the apartment at half past five. Jack is still in bed.
I start work at six. The first hour is quiet, and then the shop is busy until ten. I like the busy hours, because the time goes fast.
At half past twelve I have lunch. I eat a sandwich and I sit down for thirty minutes.
I finish at two and I am home at three. I am tired, but the apartment is quiet. I read on the green sofa, or I call my mother in Ohio.
Jack finishes at six. Today it is my turn to cook, so we have chicken and rice. We eat together and we talk about the day.
After dinner we watch TV. At ten I go to bed. Tomorrow is the same, and that's okay.

vocabulary.definition: to leave your bed in the morning
with a lot of work or a lot of people
to put your body on a chair
when you need to rest or sleep
the time when it is my job to do something
to look at something for a time

exercises.title: Understanding the Text
exercises.instructions: Read again and choose the best answer.

items.prompt: What does Emma do before she leaves home?
items.explanation: “I take a shower, I make coffee…”

items.prompt: Why does Emma like the busy hours?
items.explanation: “I like the busy hours, because the time goes fast.”

items.prompt: How long does Emma stop for lunch?
What does Emma do when she gets home?
options: She reads or telephones her mother
items.explanation: “I read on the green sofa, or I call my mother in Ohio.”
“Today it is my turn to cook.” Emma is telling the story.

items.prompt: How does Emma feel about her days?
items.explanation: “Tomorrow is the same, and that's okay. I like my days.”

exercises.title: Make the Sentence
exercises.instructions: Put the words in the correct order.

items.prompt: Say what time you get up.
Say what you do after dinner.

exercises.title: Words from All the Texts
exercises.instructions: Choose the word that matches the meaning.

items.prompt: You need to sleep. You are ___.
items.explanation: Tired is when you need to rest.

items.prompt: It is nine o'clock and Jack is ___ in bed.
items.explanation: Still means it is continuing now.

items.prompt: To telephone somebody is to ___ them.
Your friend says sorry for a small thing. You say: ___
items.explanation: That's okay means it is not a problem.

items.prompt: Yesterday Jack cooked. Today Emma cooks. Today it is ___.
items.explanation: Your turn is the time when it is your job to do something.

discussion: What time do you get up, and what time do you go to bed?
What do you do after work?
Is every day the same for you? Is that okay?
